title: Saltimbocca alla romana
intro: Veal, prosciutto and sage in a quick butter and white wine pan sauce.

steps.t: Pound the escalopes between two sheets of baking paper until thin and even.
Top each with a slice of prosciutto and a sage leaf; pin them with a toothpick.
Lightly flour only the side without prosciutto and shake off the excess.
Melt the butter in a large frying pan over medium-high heat until it foams.
Cook meat side down for 2 minutes, until golden.
steps.label: Meat side

steps.t: Flip and cook 1 minute on the prosciutto side, until the veal is no longer pink.
steps.label: Ham side

steps.t: Pour in the wine and reduce for 2 minutes until syrupy. Season lightly with salt and pepper.
steps.label: Reduce

steps.t: Remove the toothpicks and serve at once with the pan juices.

tips.t: Go easy on the salt: the prosciutto is salty and the sauce concentrates as it reduces.
Serve with garlicky sautéed spinach or chicory.

title: Ossobuco alla milanese
intro: Veal shanks braised slowly until falling off the bone, finished with gremolata.

steps.t: Snip the membrane around each shank in 3-4 places so they don't curl as they cook.
Flour, salt and brown them in butter in a wide pan, 4 minutes per side, until golden.
steps.label: Brown

steps.t: Lift out the meat, add the chopped onion, carrot and celery and cook over medium heat until soft.
steps.label: Soffritto

steps.t: Return the shanks, pour in the wine and let it bubble away.
steps.label: Deglaze

steps.t: Add hot stock (store-bought is fine) halfway up the meat, cover and simmer gently.
steps.label: Braise

pressure.t: Pressure cooker: add stock halfway up, lock the lid and cook 35 minutes at high pressure over low heat.

steps.t: Turn the shanks, add more stock if needed and cook until the meat comes away from the bone.
steps.label: Braise 2

pressure.t: Release the pressure, turn the shanks and, if the sauce is thin, reduce it uncovered for 5 minutes.

steps.t: Meanwhile, make the gremolata: finely chop the lemon zest, garlic and parsley together.
Scatter the gremolata over the shanks, cover and rest off the heat before serving.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: The classic partner is saffron risotto alla milanese.
Don't waste the marrow: spread it on toast or stir it into the risotto.
Even better the next day: reheat gently with a splash of stock.

title: Chicken cacciatore
intro: Chicken braised with tomato, red wine, rosemary and olives in a rich sauce.

steps.t: Pat the chicken dry, salt it and brown it in the oil in a wide casserole until golden all over.
steps.label: Brown

steps.t: Lift out the chicken, lower the heat and fry the sliced onion, garlic and rosemary until the onion is soft.
steps.label: Soffritto

steps.t: Return the chicken, pour in the red wine and let it bubble away.
steps.label: Deglaze

steps.t: Add the crushed tomatoes and a pinch of salt, cover and cook over low heat, turning halfway.
steps.label: Braise

oven.t: Add the tomatoes and salt, cover and bake at 170°C for 45 minutes, turning the chicken halfway.

steps.t: Stir in the olives and cook uncovered until the sauce thickens.
steps.label: Thicken

steps.t: Check it's done: the chicken should read 75°C near the bone and the juices should run clear.
Remove the rosemary, adjust the seasoning and serve with soft polenta.

tips.t: With soft polenta it's a Sunday lunch classic across central Italy.
Add 300 g button mushrooms with the olives for an autumn version.

title: Cotoletta alla milanese
intro: Bone-in veal chop, double-breaded and fried in clarified butter.

steps.t: Gently pound the meat around the bone, without detaching it, until about 1.5 cm thick.
Beat the eggs in a shallow dish and tip the breadcrumbs into another.
Dip the chops in egg, then in breadcrumbs, pressing well; repeat for a double coating.
Heat the clarified butter in a large frying pan over medium heat until it just sizzles, about 160°C.

airfryer.t: Brush both sides of the chops with melted clarified butter and preheat the air fryer to 200°C.

steps.t: Fry the first side until the crumb is hazelnut brown.
steps.label: First side

airfryer.t: Cook in the basket at 200°C for 8 minutes, without overlapping.

steps.t: Turn with a spatula and fry the other side: the meat should reach at least 63°C in the centre.
steps.label: Second side

airfryer.t: Turn and cook 6 more minutes, until golden and at least 63°C in the centre.

steps.t: Drain on kitchen paper, salt and serve straight away with lemon wedges.

tips.t: Don't detach the meat from the bone when pounding: the bone keeps it juicy.
Pounded very thin without the bone, it becomes the 'elephant ear', crisp edge to edge.
Serve with rocket and cherry tomatoes dressed with olive oil and lemon.

title: Meatballs in tomato sauce
intro: Tender meatballs simmered slowly in tomato sauce, Italian Sunday style.

steps.t: Soak the bread in the milk, then squeeze it out well.
steps.label: Soak

steps.t: Mix the meat, bread, egg, Parmigiano, parsley, salt and pepper until evenly combined.
With wet hands, shape about 20 walnut-sized meatballs.
In a wide pan, bring the tomato sauce (a good jarred one works) and the water to a simmer.
Lay the raw meatballs in the sauce without stirring, cover and cook over low heat.
steps.label: Meatballs

steps.t: Turn them gently and cook uncovered until the sauce is thick.
steps.label: Thicken

steps.t: Break one open: it must not be pink inside (72°C in the centre). Add basil and serve.

tips.t: Milk-soaked bread, not dry breadcrumbs, is what keeps them soft.
They keep 2 days in the fridge in their sauce; leftover sauce makes the next day's pasta.
Add 150 g peas for the last 10 minutes for a heartier version.

title: Chicken tikka masala
intro: Yogurt-marinated chicken, charred, in a creamy spiced tomato sauce.

steps.t: Cut the chicken into 3 cm cubes and mix with yogurt, lemon, 1 tsp garam masala, turmeric, chilli and salt.
Cover and marinate in the fridge for at least 1 hour.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.t: Spread the chicken on a lined tray and cook under the grill at 250°C until charred at the edges.
steps.label: Grill

airfryer.t: Cook the chicken in the air fryer at 200°C for 12 minutes, shaking the basket halfway.

bbq.t: Thread the chicken on skewers and cook over direct heat on the barbecue for 10 minutes, turning often.

steps.t: Meanwhile, fry the chopped onions in the oil over medium heat until golden.
steps.label: Onions

steps.t: Add grated garlic and ginger and the rest of the garam masala; stir for 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the passata and cook until thick, with the oil pooling at the edges.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Blend the sauce if you like it smooth, then add the cream and the chicken with its juices.
Simmer gently until the chicken is cooked through: 75°C in the centre, no pink inside.
steps.label: Chicken

steps.t: Scatter with coriander and serve with basmati rice or naan.

tips.t: The charred bits on the chicken give the sauce its smoky depth, so don't skip the grill.
A teaspoon of dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi) at the end makes it taste authentic.
Serve with basmati rice and a cucumber raita.

title: Beef bulgogi
intro: Korean beef marinated with pear, soy and sesame, caramelised over high heat.

steps.t: Grate the pear, garlic and ginger and mix with the soy, sugar, sesame oil and pepper.
Add the beef, sliced onion and half the sliced spring onions; massage well with your hands.
Cover and marinate in the fridge.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.t: Heat a cast-iron pan with the oil over high heat until just smoking.
Cook the beef in small batches, 2-3 minutes each, until caramelised and no longer pink.
steps.label: Pan

bbq.t: On the barbecue use a fine grill mat: cook over direct heat 2 minutes per batch, turning once.

steps.t: Scatter with the remaining spring onions and sesame; serve with rice and lettuce leaves.

tips.t: If the beef isn't pre-sliced, freeze it for 30 minutes so you can slice it paper-thin.
Wrap it in lettuce leaves with rice and kimchi, Seoul style.

title: Lemon and thyme roast chicken
intro: Crisp skin, juicy meat and potatoes roasted in the pan juices.

steps.t: Take the chicken out of the fridge and pat it very dry inside and out with kitchen paper.
steps.label: Room temp

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220°C. Cut the potatoes into wedges and toss them in the tin with 1 tbsp oil, salt and half the thyme.
Stuff the chicken with the pricked lemon, 3 garlic cloves and the rest of the thyme; tie the legs with string.
Rub the skin with the remaining oil, salt and pepper; sit it on the potatoes with the rest of the garlic and the water.
Roast at 220°C until the skin starts to colour.
steps.label: High heat

steps.t: Lower to 190°C and roast, basting halfway, until the thigh reads 75°C and the juices run clear.
steps.label: Roast

steps.t: Tent the chicken with foil and let it rest; meanwhile return the potatoes to the oven if you want them crisper.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Carve the chicken and serve with the potatoes and pan juices.

tips.t: Salt the chicken the night before and leave it uncovered in the fridge for super-crisp skin.
Use the carcass and scraps to make chicken stock for the next day.
Swap the lemon for an orange and add a few sprigs of rosemary.

title: Lamb tagine with apricots
intro: Spiced lamb slowly cooked with apricots and honey, sweet and savoury.

steps.t: Brown the lamb in the oil in a heavy casserole over medium-high heat, in batches, until golden.
steps.label: Brown

steps.t: Add the chopped onions and garlic and cook until soft.
steps.label: Onions

steps.t: Stir in the ginger, cinnamon, cumin, saffron, salt and pepper for 1 minute.
Pour in the water, bring to the boil, cover and simmer gently until the meat is tender.
steps.label: Stew

pressure.t: Pressure cooker: add the water, lock the lid and cook 35 minutes at high pressure, then release.

steps.t: Add the apricots and honey and cook uncovered until the sauce is thick and glossy.
steps.label: Apricots

steps.t: Meanwhile, toast the almonds in a dry frying pan until golden.
Serve topped with the almonds and coriander, with couscous or flatbread.

tips.t: Serve with steamed couscous dressed with a little olive oil and salt.
A teaspoon of ras el hanout instead of the single spices makes it more fragrant.
Even better the next day; it freezes well for up to 3 months.

title: Pork souvlaki with tzatziki
intro: Greek skewers marinated in lemon and oregano, with fresh tzatziki and pita.

steps.t: Cut the pork into 3 cm cubes and mix with 4 tbsp oil, lemon, oregano, 2 crushed garlic cloves, salt and pepper.
Cover and marinate in the fridge; soak the skewers in water.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.t: Meanwhile, make the tzatziki: grate the cucumber, salt it, squeeze it dry, then mix with yogurt, garlic, dill and 1 tbsp oil.
Thread the meat onto the skewers and heat a griddle pan over high heat.
Cook the skewers, turning often, until browned and the pork reaches 70°C in the centre.
steps.label: Cook

bbq.t: Cook over medium-high direct heat on the barbecue for 10 minutes, turning often, until the pork reaches 70°C.

airfryer.t: Air-fry at 200°C for 14 minutes, turning halfway, until the pork reaches 70°C.

steps.t: Warm the pitas on the griddle, 30 seconds per side.

airfryer.t: Warm the pitas in a dry frying pan, 30 seconds per side.

steps.t: Serve the skewers on the pitas with tomatoes, sliced red onion and tzatziki.

tips.t: Squeeze the cucumber hard: any water left makes the tzatziki runny.
Use boneless chicken thighs instead of pork and cook them to 75°C in the centre.

title: Lomo saltado, Peruvian beef stir-fry
intro: Beef, onion and tomato tossed in a wok with soy and vinegar, with fries and rice.

steps.t: Rinse the rice, put it in a pot with the water, a pinch of salt and a drizzle of oil; cook covered on the lowest heat.
steps.label: Rice

steps.t: Meanwhile peel the potatoes, cut into 1 cm batons, rinse and dry them very well.
Fry the potatoes in the oil at 170 °C in two batches until golden; drain on paper and salt them.
steps.label: Fries

airfryer.t: Toss the potatoes with 1 tbsp oil and air-fry at 200 °C for 20 minutes, shaking the basket now and then.

steps.t: Cut the beef into 1 x 5 cm strips and season with salt, pepper, cumin and the chopped garlic.
Cut the onions into thick wedges, the tomatoes into seeded wedges and the chili into strips.
Heat the wok until smoking with 2 tbsp oil and sear the beef in two batches until browned outside; set aside.
steps.label: Beef

steps.t: Add the remaining oil to the wok, toss the onion and chili for 1 minute, then the tomatoes for 30 seconds.
steps.label: Vegetables

steps.t: Return the beef, pour the vinegar and soy sauce down the hot sides and toss for 1 minute: there should be some juice.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Turn off the heat, add the fries and chopped cilantro, toss once and serve at once with the rice.

tips.t: Smoking-hot wok and beef in two batches: crowd it and the meat stews instead of searing.
Swap the chili for 1 tbsp ají amarillo paste from a Latin shop for a fruitier flavor.
In Peru it's washed down with cold chicha morada or a light beer.

title: Ají de gallina, creamy chili chicken
intro: Shredded chicken in a golden cream of chili, bread, walnuts and parmesan.

steps.t: Put the chicken and carrot in the cold salted water, bring to a boil and simmer until cooked through. Keep the stock.
steps.label: Chicken

steps.t: Meanwhile boil the potatoes in their skins in another pot; add the eggs for the last 9 minutes.
steps.label: Potatoes

steps.t: Soak the crustless bread in the evaporated milk and blend it with the walnuts to a smooth cream.
Separately blend the seeded pepper and chili with 50 ml of the stock to a yellow purée.
Lift out the chicken, let it cool slightly and shred it finely by hand.
In a saucepan cook the finely chopped onions in the oil over low heat until soft and golden.
steps.label: Onions

steps.t: Add the chopped garlic, pepper purée, turmeric and cumin and cook, stirring, until it thickens.
steps.label: Pepper

steps.t: Stir in the bread cream and 250 ml of stock and cook on low, stirring often, until thick and velvety.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Add the chicken and parmesan and heat for 5 minutes, loosening with stock if too thick. Season with salt and pepper.
steps.label: Chicken

steps.t: Serve over the peeled, sliced potatoes with half a hard-boiled egg and a few black olives.

tips.t: With 3 tbsp real ají amarillo paste instead of the pepper, chili and turmeric, the color is brighter.
In Peru it also comes with white rice alongside the potatoes.
It keeps 2 days in the fridge; it firms up as it cools, so reheat with a splash of stock.

title: Frango com quiabo, chicken with okra
intro: Braised chicken with seared okra, a home-cooking classic from Minas Gerais.

steps.t: Season the chicken with the lime juice, crushed garlic, salt and pepper and let it marinate.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.t: Meanwhile wash the okra, dry it thoroughly, trim the stems and cut into 1 cm rounds.
Fry the okra in a wide pan with 2 tbsp oil over high heat, stirring little, until browned and no longer slimy.
steps.label: Okra

steps.t: In a pot, brown the drained chicken in the remaining oil until golden on all sides.
steps.label: Brown

steps.t: Add the chopped onion and paprika, cook 2 minutes, then the diced tomatoes and the marinade.
steps.label: Onion

steps.t: Pour in the water, cover and simmer until the chicken is tender and cooked to the bone.
steps.label: Simmer

pressure.t: Pour in the water, lock the pressure cooker and cook 15 minutes at pressure, then release.

steps.t: Add the okra and cook uncovered until the sauce thickens.
steps.label: Okra

steps.t: Turn off the heat, scatter with chopped spring onion and parsley and serve with soft polenta or rice.

tips.t: Dry the okra well and sear it separately over high heat: it loses its slime and stays whole.
No okra? Use 400 g green beans in pieces, added raw halfway through the chicken's cooking.
In Minas it comes with angu, a soft unsalted polenta, and white rice.

title: Picanha, grilled beef rump cap
intro: The star of the churrasco: just coarse salt and its own melting fat.

steps.t: Take the meat out of the fridge 30 minutes ahead so it reaches room temperature.
steps.label: Temper

steps.t: Cut the picanha with the grain into 3 steaks 3-4 cm thick and score the fat in a diamond pattern without cutting the meat.
Just before cooking, rub the steaks with the coarse salt on all sides.
Heat the grill pan until very hot. Sear the fat side first for 4 minutes, then 4 minutes per side: 54 °C at the center for medium-rare.
steps.label: Cook

bbq.t: Over hot coals, cook the fat side 5 minutes, then 5 minutes per side, to 54 °C at the center.

pan.t: In a smoking-hot cast-iron pan without oil, cook the fat side 4 minutes, then 4 per side, to 54 °C.

steps.t: Rest the steaks on a board for 5 minutes.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Knock off excess salt, slice thinly against the grain, each slice with its fat, and serve with farofa and vinagrete.

tips.t: Cut the steaks with the grain, then slice against it to serve: that keeps it tender.
Serve with fresh vinagrete and farofa, as in every churrascaria.
Churrascaria-style: cut 3 cm slices, bend into a C with fat outside and skewer them.

title: Gà kho gừng, caramelised ginger chicken
intro: Chicken simmered in caramel with fish sauce and plenty of ginger: glossy, salty and sweet.

steps.t: Cut the chicken into bite-sized pieces and the ginger into matchsticks, and chop the shallots and garlic.
Toss the chicken with the fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, the pepper and half the garlic and shallots and marinate 20 minutes.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.t: In a wide pan heat the oil and the rest of the sugar over medium heat until it turns a deep amber caramel, 3 to 4 minutes.
steps.label: Caramel

steps.t: Immediately add the ginger and remaining garlic and shallots: they will sizzle. Stir for 30 seconds, watching for spatters.
Add the chicken with its marinade and stir until coated in caramel. Brown for 5 minutes over medium-high heat.
steps.label: Brown

steps.t: Pour in the water, cover and simmer over low heat for 15 minutes.
steps.label: Simmer

steps.t: Uncover and reduce over high heat for 7 minutes, until the sauce is sticky and glossy and the chicken is cooked through.
steps.label: Glaze

steps.t: Finish with more pepper, sliced spring onions and chili. Serve hot with steamed rice.

tips.t: Stop the caramel when it's the colour of strong tea: pale it's just sweet, near black it turns bitter.
With steamed rice and garlicky stir-fried greens it's a classic Vietnamese home dinner.

title: Larb gai, warm minced chicken salad
intro: Minced chicken with lime, mint and toasted rice powder: sour, spicy and nutty.

steps.t: Toast the sticky rice in a dry pan over medium heat for 7 minutes, shaking, until deep golden and fragrant.
steps.label: Toast rice

steps.t: Let it cool and grind to a coarse powder in a mortar or spice grinder. This is khao khua.
Thinly slice the shallots and spring onions, juice the limes and pick the mint and cilantro leaves.
Cook the chicken with the water in a pan over medium heat for 6 minutes, breaking it up, until cooked through with no pink.
steps.label: Chicken

steps.t: Off the heat add the fish sauce, lime juice, chili flakes and shallots and mix.
Stir in 2 tbsp khao khua, the spring onions, mint and cilantro. Taste: it should be sour, salty and hot.
Serve warm with lettuce leaves for wrapping and the rest of the rice powder on top.

tips.t: Eat it with sticky rice and som tam: a ball of rice, a bit of larb, a lettuce leaf.
Make a big batch of khao khua: it keeps for a month in a sealed jar.
Made with ground pork it becomes larb moo, the other great Isan classic.

title: Gaeng khiao wan gai, green curry
intro: Chicken and eggplant in coconut milk with green curry paste, Thai basil and makrut lime.

steps.t: Cut the eggplant into 3 cm chunks and the chicken into thin slices.
In a wok heat the oil with 150 ml of the thickest coconut cream from the can and cook 3 minutes, until the oil separates.
steps.label: Coconut

steps.t: Add the curry paste and fry for 2 minutes, stirring, until very fragrant.
steps.label: Curry paste

steps.t: Add the chicken, turn it well in the paste and cook for 3 minutes.
steps.label: Chicken

steps.t: Pour in the rest of the coconut milk, add the eggplant, bamboo, torn lime leaves, fish sauce and sugar and simmer 12 minutes.
steps.label: Curry

steps.t: Check the eggplant is soft and the chicken cooked through, then adjust with fish sauce and sugar.
Turn off the heat, stir in the basil and sliced chili and serve straight away.

tips.t: Serve with steamed jasmine rice: the curry is soupy and meant to be spooned over it.
Ready-made pastes vary a lot in heat: start with 2 tbsp and add more after tasting.
With the small round green Thai eggplants from Asian shops, quartered, it tastes like Bangkok.

title: Kibbeh bil sayniyeh (baked kibbeh)
intro: A bulgur and meat shell around minced meat, onion and pine nuts, baked in a tray.

ing.n: extra virgin olive oil for the top

steps.t: Rinse the bulgur, cover with cold water for 15 minutes, then squeeze it dry between your hands.
steps.label: Bulgur

steps.t: Meanwhile, for the filling, toast the pine nuts in the oil until golden and lift out. In the same pan soften the chopped onions.
steps.label: Onions

steps.t: Add the ground beef, half the spices, salt and pepper and brown, breaking it up, until cooked. Stir in the pine nuts and let cool.
steps.label: Filling

steps.t: For the shell, blitz the onion with the rest of the spices and salt, then add the lean beef, bulgur and ice water to a smooth paste.
Heat the oven to 200 °C. Oil a 28 cm round tray and press half the shell into a 1 cm layer with wet hands.
Spread over the filling and cover with the remaining shell, flattened into patties between wet hands and joined. Smooth the top.
Score a diamond pattern down to the filling, make a hole in the centre and pour over the oil.
Bake at 200 °C for 35 minutes, until deep brown and crisp at the edges.
steps.label: Oven

steps.t: Rest for 10 minutes, then cut along the scored lines. Serve with yogurt and a salad.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Keep the meat and water very cold and use very lean meat: the shell stays firm and won't crack.
In Lebanon it's often made with lean lamb, which tastes richer.
Serve with yogurt and cucumber with mint, or with fattoush.

title: Shish tawouk with toum
intro: Chicken skewers marinated in yogurt, lemon and garlic, with Lebanese garlic sauce.

steps.t: Mix the yogurt, lemon juice, the 3 grated garlic cloves, tomato paste, paprika, allspice, oil, salt and pepper.
Cut the chicken into 3 cm cubes, toss in the marinade, cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours (overnight is best).
steps.label: Marinade

steps.t: Meanwhile make the toum: blend the garlic cloves, germ removed, with a pinch of salt for 1 minute to a paste.
With the motor running, add the oil in a thin stream, alternating with lemon juice and ice water, until white, thick and fluffy.
Thread the chicken onto the skewers (if wooden, soaked in water for 30 minutes) without packing the pieces too tightly.
Cook on a very hot grill pan for 12 minutes, turning often, until golden and cooked through with no pink inside.
steps.label: Skewers

bbq.t: Cook over hot coals for 10 minutes, turning often, until golden and cooked through with no pink inside.

oven.t: Cook under the oven grill at 220 °C for 18 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and cooked through.

steps.t: Serve with the toum, warm pita and pickles.

tips.t: Remove the garlic germ and add the oil very slowly: the toum emulsifies without splitting.
Leftover toum keeps for 2 weeks in a closed jar in the fridge.
With fattoush and batata harra it becomes a full Lebanese dinner.

title: Kefta tagine with eggs
intro: Spiced little meatballs in tomato sauce with eggs cooked on top, eaten with bread.

steps.t: Grate the onion. Knead the meat with half the onion, half the chopped herbs, 1 tsp cumin, 1 tsp paprika, salt and pepper.
With wet hands roll walnut-sized meatballs, about 30.
In a wide lidded pan warm the oil with the rest of the onion and the chopped garlic until soft.
steps.label: Soften

steps.t: Add the crushed tomatoes, the remaining spices, chili and salt and cook until the sauce thickens.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Lay the meatballs in the sauce in a single layer, cover and cook, shaking the pan now and then.
steps.label: Kefta

steps.t: Make 4 hollows, crack an egg into each, cover and cook until the whites are set and the yolks still soft.
steps.label: Eggs

steps.t: Scatter with the remaining herbs and a pinch of cumin and serve in the pan, with bread to scoop up the sauce.

tips.t: Keep wetting your hands with cold water as you shape the kefta: they stay smooth and don't stick.
Half beef, half lamb makes it taste even more Moroccan.
In Morocco it's eaten without cutlery, scooping up sauce and egg with khobz.

title: Kung pao chicken with peanuts
intro: Chicken with dried chillies and peanuts in a sweet-sour sauce, a Sichuan classic.

steps.t: Cut the chicken into 1.5 cm cubes and mix with 1 tbsp soy, the wine and 3 tsp cornflour. Leave to marinate.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.t: Meanwhile mix the rest of the soy with the vinegar, sugar, last tsp of cornflour and water. Snap the chillies and shake out the seeds.
Heat the oil in the wok over medium heat and fry the chillies and Sichuan pepper until they just darken, without burning.
steps.label: Chillies

steps.t: Turn up the heat, add the chicken and stir-fry until golden and cooked right through.
steps.label: Chicken

steps.t: Add the sliced garlic and ginger and the spring onions cut into chunks; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Stir the sauce and pour it in: within seconds it turns thick and glossy. Turn off the heat and toss in the peanuts.
Serve straight away with plain rice; the chillies are there for aroma, not for eating.

tips.t: Add the peanuts off the heat so they stay crunchy all the way to the table.
No black vinegar? Use rice vinegar with half a teaspoon of balsamic.

title: Hong shao rou, red-braised pork belly
intro: Pork belly caramelised and braised with soy and star anise until it melts in the mouth.

steps.t: Cut the belly into 3 cm cubes, cover with cold water, bring to the boil and cook for 3 minutes. Drain and rinse.
steps.label: Blanch

steps.t: In a heavy pot heat the oil and sugar over low heat, stirring, until it turns into an amber caramel.
steps.label: Caramel

steps.t: Add the well-dried pork and turn it until glossy and mahogany-coloured. Watch out for spatters.
steps.label: Brown

steps.t: Add the sliced ginger, spring onions in pieces, star anise and cinnamon; splash in the wine and add both soy sauces.
Pour in hot water to just cover, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat, stirring now and then.
steps.label: Braise

pressure.t: In a pressure cooker, just cover with hot water, lock the lid and cook for 25 minutes at pressure, then release.

steps.t: Remove the aromatics, uncover and turn up the heat: reduce, stirring, until the sauce is syrupy and glazes the pork.
steps.label: Reduce

steps.t: Serve hot with plain rice and a spoonful of the sauce.

tips.t: Dry the pork well before it goes into the caramel: it spatters less and colours more evenly.
Add 4 peeled hard-boiled eggs for the last half hour: they take on colour and soak up the sauce.
It's even better the next day: lift off the set fat and reheat gently with a splash of water.

title: Jjimdak, Andong braised chicken
intro: Chicken braised in a sweet, spicy soy sauce with potatoes and glassy sweet potato noodles.

steps.t: Soak the sweet potato noodles in lukewarm water.
steps.label: Soak

steps.t: Meanwhile blanch the chicken in boiling water, then drain and rinse it: the sauce will stay clean.
steps.label: Chicken

steps.t: Mix the soy, sugar, honey, mirin, minced garlic, grated ginger, pepper and water.
Put the chicken, sauce and chillies in a wide pot, bring to the boil, cover and cook over medium-low heat.
steps.label: Braise

steps.t: Add the potatoes and carrot in big chunks and the onion wedges; cover and cook until the potatoes are tender and the chicken cooked through.
steps.label: Vegetables

steps.t: Add the drained noodles and spring onions in pieces; cook uncovered, stirring, until the noodles are glossy and have soaked up the sauce.
steps.label: Noodles

steps.t: Drizzle with sesame oil, sprinkle with sesame seeds and set the pot in the middle of the table.

tips.t: The noodles drink a lot of liquid: if the sauce dries out, add a ladle of water.
In Andong they use jocheong rice syrup instead of honey; look for it in Korean shops.

title: Shōgayaki, Japanese ginger pork
intro: Pork stir-fried in a fresh ginger and soy sauce, served with crisp raw cabbage.

steps.t: Finely grate the ginger and stir it into the soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar until the sugar dissolves.
Nick the fatty edge of each slice in 2 or 3 places so it doesn't curl, then leave in the marinade for 10 minutes.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.t: Meanwhile shred the cabbage very finely, soak it in iced water for 5 minutes to crisp up and drain well.
Slice the onion. Heat the oil in a wide pan over high heat and stir-fry the onion for 2 minutes until softened.
steps.label: Onion

steps.t: Drain the pork (keep the marinade) and cook in a single layer over high heat, 90 seconds per side, until no longer pink.
steps.label: Pork

steps.t: Pour in the marinade and toss for 1 minute, until the sauce reduces and glazes the pork and onion.
steps.label: Glaze

steps.t: Serve with a mound of raw cabbage, the sauce spooned over the pork, and plain rice.

tips.t: Grate the ginger at the last minute and keep a teaspoon back to add at the end: more aroma.
Lightly dust the slices with potato starch: the sauce clings better and stays glossy.
With rice, kenchinjiru and a cold side, it's a complete Japanese home meal.

title: İzmir köfte, baked meatballs
intro: Köfte, potatoes and green peppers baked in tomato sauce, the Izmir way.

steps.t: Soak the bread in water and squeeze it out. Grate the onion and squeeze out its juice; chop the garlic and parsley.
Knead everything with the beef, cumin, salt and pepper for 3 minutes, until sticky. Rest in the fridge for 20 minutes.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Meanwhile peel the potatoes, cut into thick wedges and pat them dry. Slice the tomatoes.
Fry the potatoes in the hot oil for 8 minutes, turning, until golden outside but not fully cooked.
steps.label: Potatoes

airfryer.t: Toss the potatoes with a little oil and air-fry at 200 °C for 15 minutes, shaking the basket halfway.

steps.t: With damp hands, shape 12 oblong köfte 8 cm long and brown them in the same pan for 5 minutes, until golden all over.
steps.label: Köfte

airfryer.t: Shape 12 oblong köfte 8 cm long and air-fry at 200 °C for 8 minutes, turning halfway.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 200 °C. In a baking dish, line up köfte, potatoes, whole peppers and tomato slices in tight alternating rows.
Dissolve the tomato paste in the hot water with a pinch of salt and pepper and pour it into the dish.
Bake for 35 minutes, until the sauce has reduced, the peppers are blistered and the köfte are cooked through.
steps.label: Oven

steps.t: Rest for 5 minutes and serve from the dish, with bread or rice pilaf for the sauce.

tips.t: Squeeze the grated onion well: its juice would make the köfte fall apart.
Half beef, half lamb gives the flavour of Izmir's home-style restaurants.
Serve with bulgur pilaf and cold ayran, as they do in Turkey.

title: Tavuk şiş, chicken skewers
intro: Chicken thigh skewers marinated in yogurt and chilli, tender inside and charred outside.

steps.t: Cut the chicken into 3 cm cubes. In a bowl, mix the yogurt, tomato paste, oil, grated garlic, juice of 1 lemon, spices, salt and pepper.
Coat the chicken in the marinade, cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours. Soak the skewers in water.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.t: Thread 5 or 6 pieces onto each skewer, snug but not squashed. Take the chicken out of the fridge 15 minutes ahead.
Heat the grill pan well and oil it. Cook the skewers for 13 minutes, turning every 3, until charred at the edges and cooked through.
steps.label: Skewers

oven.t: Cook on the top rack under the oven grill at 230 °C for 20 minutes, turning halfway, until cooked through.

bbq.t: Cook over hot coals for 11 minutes, turning often, until charred at the edges with no pink inside.

steps.t: Rest for 3 minutes, then squeeze over the other lemon and serve with lavash or rice.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Thighs stay juicy even over high heat; breast dries out quickly.
Serve with çoban salatası, sumac red onion and cold ayran.
Wrapped in lavash with onion, parsley and sumac, they become a dürüm.

title: Mole poblano with chicken
intro: Puebla's festive sauce of dried chilies, nuts, spices and chocolate over chicken.

steps.t: Put the chicken in the water with half the onion, 1 garlic clove and salt; bring to a boil and simmer until cooked through.
steps.label: Chicken

steps.t: Meanwhile stem and seed the chilies, saving 1 tbsp seeds, toast 20 seconds per side and soak in hot water.
steps.label: Chilies

steps.t: In 1 tbsp lard toast the almonds, peanuts, 3 tbsp sesame, chili seeds, cloves, aniseed and pepper until golden.
steps.label: Toasting

steps.t: In the same pan, let the raisins puff for a few seconds, then fry the torn tortilla until crisp.
Char the tomatoes, the other half onion and 2 garlic cloves in the pan until blackened in spots.
steps.label: Tomatoes

steps.t: Blend everything with the drained chilies, cinnamon and 500 ml of the chicken broth until very smooth; strain.
Heat 2 tbsp lard in a heavy pot, pour in the sauce (it spatters) and fry, stirring, until it darkens.
steps.label: Mole

steps.t: Add the chocolate, sugar and 250 ml broth; simmer on low, stirring often, until it coats a spoon. Salt to taste.
steps.label: Mole

steps.t: Add the drained chicken pieces and let them heat through in the sauce over low heat.
steps.label: Chicken

steps.t: Serve the chicken smothered in mole, sprinkle with the remaining sesame and add rice and warm tortillas.

tips.t: If you find mulato chilies in a Latin shop, swap 2 anchos: it is the classic mole poblano trio.
With Mexican table chocolate, already sweet and spiced with cinnamon, leave out the sugar.
Leftover mole freezes well; spooned over chicken-filled tortillas it becomes enmoladas.

title: Cochinita pibil
intro: Yucatán pork marinated in achiote and citrus, slow-cooked and pulled.

steps.t: Blend the achiote with the juice of the oranges and 2 limes, garlic, cumin, 1 tsp oregano, pepper and salt.
Cut the meat into 6 large pieces, coat them in the marinade, cover and refrigerate (overnight is fine).
steps.label: Marinade

steps.t: Heat the oven to 160 °C. Line a dish with baking paper and foil, add meat and marinade and seal into a parcel.

pressure.t: Put the meat and marinade in the pressure cooker with 100 ml water and lock the lid.

steps.t: Bake until the meat falls apart with a fork.
steps.label: Oven

pressure.t: Cook 60 minutes at pressure over low heat, then let the pressure drop naturally.

steps.t: Meanwhile thinly slice the red onions and toss with the juice of 3 limes, salt, oregano and the sliced chili.
steps.label: Onions

steps.t: Shred the meat with two forks right in its juices and adjust the salt.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan 30 seconds per side, fill with the pork and top with the pickled onions.

tips.t: Bitter Seville orange juice instead of orange and lime makes it taste just like in Yucatán.
Banana leaves from an Asian shop, briefly passed over a flame, give the meat a grassy aroma.
The real Yucatán chili is the habanero: use only half, it is very hot.

title: Chiles en nogada
intro: It is said they were created in Puebla in 1821, in the colours of the Mexican flag.

steps.t: Char the peppers under the oven grill at 250 °C, turning, until the skin is black and blistered.
steps.label: Peppers

steps.t: Seal them in a bowl covered with cling film: the steam loosens the skin.
steps.label: Steam

steps.t: Meanwhile cover the walnuts with boiling water, then rub them between your fingers to remove as much skin as you can.
steps.label: Walnuts

steps.t: Blend the walnuts, milk, goat cheese, sugar and a pinch of salt into a smooth, pourable sauce; chill it.
Peel the peppers, slit them lengthwise and remove the seeds and ribs, keeping them whole.
Sauté the chopped onion and garlic in the oil, then add the meat and brown it, breaking it up.
steps.label: Meat

steps.t: Add grated tomatoes, diced apple, pear and peach, raisins, chopped almonds, cinnamon, salt and pepper; cook until dry.
steps.label: Filling

steps.t: Stuff the peppers with the picadillo and close them slightly.
Serve them lukewarm, covered with cold nogada and topped with pomegranate seeds and parsley leaves.

tips.t: With real poblano chilies from a Latin shop the flavour is more fragrant and slightly hot.
For the capeado version, dip the stuffed peppers in whisked egg batter and fry them.

title: Stifado (beef with pearl onions)
intro: Beef braised in red wine with pearl onions, cinnamon and allspice, sweet and fragrant.

steps.t: Blanch the pearl onions for 2 minutes, cool them in cold water and peel, keeping them whole.
steps.label: Onions

steps.t: In a heavy pot brown the beef over high heat in 4 tbsp oil, in batches, until well browned.
steps.label: Browning

steps.t: Add the garlic and tomato paste, stir 1 minute, then deglaze with wine and vinegar and let it bubble off.
Add the crushed tomatoes, cinnamon, cloves, allspice, bay, water, salt and pepper; cover and simmer gently.
steps.label: Braise

pressure.t: Add tomatoes, spices, bay, water, salt and pepper, lock the pressure cooker and cook 25 minutes at pressure.

steps.t: Meanwhile brown the whole pearl onions in the remaining oil, shaking the pan, until golden all over.
steps.label: Onions

steps.t: Add the onions to the beef without stirring, shake the pot and cook covered until the beef is very tender.
steps.label: Braise

pressure.t: Open, add the onions without stirring, lock again and cook another 10 minutes at pressure.

steps.t: Remove the cinnamon and bay, let it rest 10 minutes and serve with crusty bread, rice or potatoes.

tips.t: Once the onions are in, do not stir: shake the pot and they stay whole and glossy.
Use jointed rabbit instead of beef for kouneli stifado, an island classic.
It is even better the next day: reheat gently with a splash of water.

title: Paidakia (Greek lamb chops)
intro: Grilled lamb chops with lemon and oregano, just like in a Greek taverna.

steps.t: Rub the chops with oil, the juice of 1 lemon, crushed garlic, half the oregano and pepper; leave to marinate.
steps.label: Marinade

steps.t: Heat the grill pan until it is smoking hot.

bbq.t: Light the barbecue and get the coals glowing hot.

pan.t: Heat a cast-iron pan over high heat with a drizzle of oil.

steps.t: Salt the chops only now, just before cooking.
Cook 3-4 minutes per side until well browned outside and pink inside.
steps.label: Grill

bbq.t: Grill over the coals 3 minutes per side until charred outside and pink inside.

pan.t: Pan-fry 4 minutes per side without crowding until golden.

steps.t: Let them rest a few minutes, then squeeze over lemon and sprinkle with the remaining oregano and flaky salt.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Serve straight away with lemon wedges: in Greece they are eaten with your hands.

tips.t: Serve with tzatziki and oregano fries, taverna style.
Use Greek rigani, wild oregano sold in bunches: it is far more fragrant.
Ask for chops 1.5 cm thick: they cook fast and stay pink and juicy.

title: Rogan josh, Kashmiri lamb curry
intro: Lamb slowly braised in a red sauce of yogurt, fennel and ginger, with no onion at all.

steps.t: Cut the lamb into 4 cm chunks, pat dry with paper towels and season with salt.
Whisk the yogurt with the paprika, chili powder and 100 ml of the water until smooth.
Heat the oil well in a heavy pot and fry the cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, bay leaves and asafoetida for 30 seconds.
steps.label: Spices

steps.t: Turn up the heat, add the lamb and brown it well on all sides, in two batches if needed.
steps.label: Brown

steps.t: Lower the heat and add the yogurt a spoonful at a time, stirring, until the oil rises to the surface.
steps.label: Yogurt

steps.t: Add the fennel, ginger and remaining water, cover and simmer gently until the lamb is very tender.
steps.label: Braise

pressure.t: In a pressure cooker: seal and cook for 25 minutes at pressure, then let the pressure drop naturally.

steps.t: Uncover, stir in the garam masala and reduce until the sauce is thick and glossy with red oil.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Take off the heat, let it rest a few minutes and serve with basmati rice or naan.

tips.t: Use room-temperature yogurt and add it slowly over low heat so it doesn't split.
Kashmiri chili and mustard oil from Indian shops give a redder, milder and more authentic sauce.
Serve with cumin jeera rice and warm naan to mop up the sauce.

title: Pollo al ajillo, Spanish garlic chicken
intro: Chicken pieces browned in olive oil with lots of unpeeled garlic, white wine and bay.

steps.t: Season the chicken with salt and pepper and leave it at room temperature while you prep the rest.
Lightly crush the garlic cloves with the flat of a knife, leaving the skins on.
Heat the oil in a wide casserole and fry the garlic over medium heat until golden, then lift it out.
steps.label: Garlic

steps.t: In the same oil brown the chicken skin side down, turning, until golden on all sides.
steps.label: Brown

steps.t: Return the garlic, add the bay and chili, deglaze with the wine, scraping the bottom, and let it bubble off.
steps.label: Wine

steps.t: Cover and cook over low heat, turning once, until the meat by the bone is no longer pink and the juices run clear.
steps.label: Cook

steps.t: Uncover and turn up the heat until the sauce reduces to a glossy, oily glaze.
steps.label: Reduce

steps.t: Scatter with chopped parsley and serve with bread to mop up the sauce.

tips.t: Keep the skins on the garlic: they protect the cloves, which turn soft and sweet enough to spread on bread.
Swap the wine for a dry fino or manzanilla sherry, as they do in Andalusia.
Serve with fries or patatas bravas and a green salad.

title: Bœuf bourguignon
intro: Beef braised in red wine with lardons, mushrooms and pearl onions: a Burgundy classic.

steps.t: Cut the beef into 5 cm cubes, pat it very dry with paper towels and season with salt and pepper.
In a cast-iron casserole, brown the pancetta in 1 tbsp oil until golden, then set it aside.
steps.label: Pancetta

steps.t: Add the remaining oil and brown the beef in two batches over high heat until deeply browned all over. Set aside.
steps.label: Browning

steps.t: Lower the heat and cook the sliced carrots, chopped onion and crushed garlic until soft.
steps.label: Vegetables

steps.t: Return the beef and pancetta, sprinkle with the flour, add the tomato paste and stir for 2 minutes.
steps.label: Flour

steps.t: Pour in the wine and stock, add the thyme and bay leaves and bring to a boil, scraping the bottom.
Cover and simmer on the lowest heat for 2 and a half hours, until the beef falls apart with a fork.
steps.label: Braise

pressure.t: Lock the pressure cooker lid and cook for 45 minutes at pressure, then let it release naturally.

steps.t: Meanwhile, near the end, brown the peeled pearl onions in half the butter until golden and tender.
steps.label: Pearl onions

steps.t: Add the remaining butter and the halved mushrooms and sauté over high heat until golden.
steps.label: Mushrooms

steps.t: Remove the thyme and bay, stir the mushrooms and onions into the stew and simmer uncovered until the sauce coats a spoon.
steps.label: Reduce

steps.t: Scatter with parsley and serve with boiled potatoes, mash or buttered noodles.

tips.t: Make it a day ahead: after a night in the fridge it tastes even better. Reheat gently, covered.
Marinating the beef overnight in the wine with carrot, onion and thyme gives a deeper sauce.
Serve with buttery Vichy carrots and a red Burgundy at 16 °C, the same wine you cooked with.

title: Coq au vin
intro: Chicken simmered in red wine with lardons, mushrooms and pearl onions in a glossy sauce.

ing.n: full-bodied red wine (Pinot Noir or Burgundy)

steps.t: Pat the chicken dry and season it. In a casserole, fry the pancetta in the oil until crisp, then lift it out.
steps.label: Pancetta

steps.t: Brown the chicken in the fat left in the pan, skin side first, until deep golden. Pour off excess fat.
steps.label: Chicken

steps.t: Pour in the cognac and flambé it with a long match, extractor fan off, or simply let it bubble away.
Lift out the chicken, cook the chopped onion, carrot and garlic until soft, then stir in the flour and tomato paste.
steps.label: Vegetables

steps.t: Return the chicken and pancetta, pour in the wine and stock (shop-bought is fine), add thyme and bay and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 1 hour, until the meat comes away from the bone and reaches 75 °C inside.
steps.label: Simmer

pressure.t: Lock the pressure cooker and cook for 18 minutes at pressure; release and check the meat comes off the bone.

steps.t: Meanwhile, brown the peeled pearl onions in half the butter in a frying pan until golden and tender.
steps.label: Pearl onions

steps.t: Add the rest of the butter and the halved mushrooms and sauté over high heat until golden.
steps.label: Mushrooms

steps.t: Lift out the chicken and boil the sauce hard until it coats a spoon; return the chicken, mushrooms and onions.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Discard the thyme and bay, scatter with parsley and serve with boiled potatoes or crusty bread.

tips.t: Leave the chicken overnight in the wine with onion and thyme: tastier meat and a darker sauce.
Use Riesling instead of red wine and finish with a splash of cream for Alsatian coq au riesling.
It is even better the next day: reheat over low heat with a splash of water.

title: Buttermilk fried chicken
intro: Chicken soaked in buttermilk and fried in a craggy, spiced crust, Southern style.

ing.n: bone-in, skin-on chicken thighs and drumsticks

steps.t: In a bowl, whisk the yogurt, milk, hot sauce and 2 tsp salt: this is your buttermilk.
Add the chicken, cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours, ideally overnight.
steps.label: Marinate

steps.t: In a wide bowl, mix the flour, cornstarch, baking powder, paprika, garlic powder, cayenne, pepper and remaining salt.
Drizzle 3 tbsp of the marinade into the flour and rub it in with your fingers: those little clumps make the crunchy crust.
Lift the chicken from the marinade, press it firmly into the flour and let it rest on a wire rack.
steps.label: Rest

steps.t: Heat the oil to 170 °C in a deep, heavy pot filled no more than halfway.

airfryer.t: Preheat the air fryer to 190 °C and spray the chicken lightly with oil on all sides.

oven.t: Heat a fan oven to 220 °C, set a rack over a baking tray and spray the chicken with oil on all sides.

steps.t: Fry a few pieces at a time, turning, keeping the oil at 150-160 °C, until deep golden and 75 °C inside.
steps.label: Frying

airfryer.t: Cook in a single layer at 190 °C for 25 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and 75 °C inside.

oven.t: Bake on the rack for 45 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and 75 °C inside.

steps.t: Drain the chicken on a rack, sprinkle with a little salt and let it rest before serving.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: With real buttermilk it is even simpler: use 450 ml instead of the yogurt and milk.
Add 1 tsp dried thyme and 1 tsp dried oregano to the flour, as many Southern cooks do.
Serve with coleslaw, cornbread and a drizzle of hot honey.
